That streams raw ephys over the network and is not\\\\n    used by any downstream computation, so it is skipped.\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    spikes_list, clusters_list = [], []\\\\n    for pid, pname in zip(pids, pnames):\\\\n        ssl = SpikeSortingLoader(pid=str(pid), one=one, eid=eid, pname=pname)\\\\n        sp, cl, ch = ssl.load_spike_sorting()\\\\n        if len(sp) == 0 or len(cl) == 0:\\\\n            continue\\\\n        cld = SpikeSortingLoader.merge_clusters(sp, cl, ch).to_df()\\\\n        cld['pid'] = str(pid)\\\\n        spikes_list.append(sp)\\\\n        clusters_list.append(cld)\\\\n    if not spikes_list:\\\\n        raise RuntimeError('no spike sorting could be loaded for this session')\\\\n    if len(spikes_list) == 1:\\\\n        return spikes_list[0], clusters_list[0]\\\\n    return merge_probes(spikes_list, clusters_list)\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef select_neurons(clusters, brain_regions):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Apply the data paper's neuron and region inclusion criteria.\\\\n\\\\n    * `label >= 1` keeps only \\\\\\\"well-isolated neurons\\\\\\\": in `ibllib`, `label` is the fraction\\\\n      of the three RIGOR single-unit metrics a cluster passes (amplitude > 50 uV,\\\\n      noise cut-off < 20 uV, refractory-period violation), so `label == 1` is exactly the\\\\n      data paper's criterion.\\\\n    * Beryl acronyms `root` / `void` are dropped, implementing the data paper's restriction\\\\n      to regions \\\\\\\"designated grey matter in the adult mouse Allen CCF\\\\\\\". The reference code\\\\n      makes the same exclusion in `MultiRegionDataModule.list_regions`.\\\\n\\\\n    Returns (keep_idx, beryl_acronyms_of_kept_neurons).\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    beryl = np.asarray(brain_regions.acronym2acronym(\\\\n        clusters['acronym'].to_numpy(), mapping='Beryl'))\\\\n    good = clusters['label'].to_numpy() >= QC_LABEL\\\\n    grey = ~np.isin(beryl, NON_GREY_MATTER)\\\\n    keep = np.nonzero(good & grey)[0]\\\\n    return keep, beryl[keep]\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef bin_spiking_data_fast(spike_times, spike_clusters, n_clusters, align_times):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Bin spikes into (n_trials, n_clusters, NBINS) counts.\\\\n\\\\n    Vectorised equivalent of the reference `bin_spiking_data` /\\\\n    `get_spike_data_per_interval`, which calls `iblutil.numerical.bincount2D` once per\\\\n    trial inside a multiprocessing pool. `bincount2D` assigns a sample to bin\\\\n    `floor((t - t_beg) / binsize)` over `[t_beg, t_end]` and the reference then truncates\\\\n    to the first `NBINS` columns, so a spike landing exactly on `t_end` is dropped. The\\\\n    same convention is reproduced here (spikes are taken from `[t_beg, t_end)` and bin\\\\n    indices outside `[0, NBINS)` are discarded).\\\\n\\\\n    Args:\\\\n        spike_times: (n_spikes,) spike times, sorted ascending.\\\\n        spike_clusters: (n_spikes,) cluster index in `[0, n_clusters)`.\\\\n        n_clusters: number of neurons.\\\\n        align_times: (n_trials,) alignment event times.\\\\n\\\\n    Returns:\\\\n        (n_trials, n_clusters, NBINS) uint8 array of spike counts.\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    beg = align_times + TIME_WINDOW[0]\\\\n    end = align_times + TIME_WINDOW[1]\\\\n    out = np.zeros((len(align_times), n_clusters, NBINS), dtype=np.uint8)\\\\n    finite = np.isfinite(beg) & np.isfinite(end)\\\\n    i0 = np.searchsorted(spike_times, np.where(finite, beg, np.inf), side='left')\\\\n    i1 = np.searchsorted(spike_times, np.where(finite, end, np.inf), side='left')\\\\n    for k in range(len(align_times)):\\\\n        if not finite[k]:\\\\n            continue\\\\n        t = spike_times[i0[k]:i1[k]]\\\\n        c = spike_clusters[i0[k]:i1[k]]\\\\n        b = np.floor((t - beg[k]) / BINSIZE).astype(np.int64)\\\\n        ok = (b >= 0) & (b < NBINS)\\\\n        counts = np.bincount(c[ok] * NBINS + b[ok], minlength=n_clusters * NBINS)\\\\n        np.clip(counts, 0, 255, out=counts)\\\\n        out[k] = counts.reshape(n_clusters, NBINS).astype(np.uint8)\\\\n    return out\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\\\n# Behaviour\\\\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\\\ndef load_dynamic_behaviour(sess_loader):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Load the two time-varying behaviours the decoder has to predict.\\\\n\\\\n    Reproduces `ibl_data_utils.load_target_behavior`:\\\\n      * wheel speed  = |velocity| of the uniformly resampled (~1 kHz) wheel trace,\\\\n      * whisker motion energy = `whiskerMotionEnergy` of the **left** camera (60 Hz),\\\\n        falling back to the right camera (150 Hz) when the left one is unavailable --\\\\n        exactly the fallback in `ibl_data_utils.bin_behaviors`.\\\\n\\\\n    Returns {'wheel-speed': (times, values), 'whisker-motion-energy': (times, values)},\\\\n    plus the camera actually used.\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    out = {}\\\\n    sess_loader.load_wheel()\\\\n    out['wheel-speed'] = (sess_loader.wheel['times'].to_numpy(),\\\\n                          np.abs(sess_loader.wheel['velocity'].to_numpy()))\\\\n\\\\n    camera_used = None\\\\n    for view, key in (('left', 'leftCamera'), ('right', 'rightCamera')):\\\\n        try:\\\\n            sess_loader.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\\\\n            me = sess_loader.motion_energy[key]\\\\n            times = me['times'].to_numpy()\\\\n            vals = me['whiskerMotionEnergy'].to_numpy()\\\\n            if len(times) == 0 or np.all(np.isnan(vals)):\\\\n                continue\\\\n            out['whisker-motion-energy'] = (times, vals)\\\\n            camera_used = view\\\\n            break\\\\n        except Exception:\\\\n            continue\\\\n    if camera_used is None:\\\\n        raise RuntimeError('no whisker motion energy available')\\\\n    return out, camera_used\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef bin_behaviour_per_trial(target_times, target_vals, align_times):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Resample a behavioural trace onto the 100 trial bins, per trial.\\\\n\\\\n    Faithful re-implementation of `ibl_data_utils.get_behavior_per_interval`:\\\\n      * the trace is sliced to the open interval (t_beg, t_end),\\\\n      * a trial is rejected when there is no data, when the trace starts more than one bin\\\\n        after `t_beg` or ends more than one bin before `t_end`, when the interval time is\\\\n        NaN, or when the slice contains NaNs,\\\\n      * the remaining trials are linearly interpolated (with linear extrapolation at the\\\\n        edges) onto `np.linspace(t_beg + binsize, t_end, n_bins)`, i.e. the right edge of\\\\n        each bin.\\\\n\\\\n    The only deviation is that NaNs always reject a trial (the reference's\\\\n    `allow_nans=False` branch). The reference caching script passes `allow_nans=True` and\\\\n    lets the model impute NaNs with the trial average at fit time; here the converted\\\\n    outputs must be valid class labels at every timepoint, and `verify_data_format`\\\\n    rejects NaNs outright, so NaN-containing trials are dropped instead.\\\\n\\\\n    Returns (values (n_trials, NBINS) float64 with NaN rows for rejected trials,\\\\n             good mask (n_trials,) bool).\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    n = len(align_times)\\\\n    vals = np.full((n, NBINS), np.nan)\\\\n    good = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)\\\\n\\\\n    beg = align_times + TIME_WINDOW[0]\\\\n    end = align_times + TIME_WINDOW[1]\\\\n    finite = np.isfinite(beg) & np.isfinite(end)\\\\n    if not np.any(finite):\\\\n        return vals, good\\\\n\\\\n    idx_beg = np.searchsorted(target_times, np.where(finite, beg, np.inf), side='right')\\\\n    idx_end = np.searchsorted(target_times, np.where(finite, end, np.inf), side='left')\\\\n\\\\n    for k in range(n):\\\\n        if not finite[k]:\\\\n            continue\\\\n        tt = target_times[idx_beg[k]:idx_end[k]]\\\\n        tv = target_vals[idx_beg[k]:idx_end[k]]\\\\n        if len(tv) == 0:\\\\n            continue\\\\n        if np.isnan(tv).any():\\\\n            continue\\\\n        if abs(beg[k] - tt[0]) > BINSIZE:      # target data starts too late\\\\n            continue\\\\n        if abs(end[k] - tt[-1]) > BINSIZE:     # target data ends too early\\\\n            continue\\\\n        x = np.linspace(beg[k] + BINSIZE, end[k], NBINS)\\\\n        vals[k] = interp1d(tt, tv, kind='linear', fill_value='extrapolate')(x)\\\\n        good[k] = True\\\\n    return vals, good\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef discretize_tertiles(values):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Discretize a continuous time-varying behaviour into 3 equal-occupancy bins.\\\\n\\\\n    Thresholds are the 33.3rd and 66.7th percentiles of every retained (trial, time-bin)\\\\n    sample of **that session**. Per-session thresholds are used because both signals are in\\\\n    session-specific units: whisker motion energy is an uncalibrated pixel-intensity\\\\n    difference whose scale depends on the camera (left 1280x1024 @60 Hz vs right 640x512\\\\n    @150 Hz), on illumination and on ROI placement, and wheel-speed statistics depend on how\\\\n    vigorously a given mouse turns the wheel. A single global threshold would map whole\\\\n    sessions into one class; per-session tertiles give ~1/3 of samples per class in every\\\\n    session, so chance is a well-defined 1/3 and the shared decoder sees a comparable\\\\n    target in every session.\\\\n\\\\n    Returns (labels (int) in {0,1,2}, thresholds (2,)).\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    finite = values[np.isfinite(values)]\\\\n    thresholds = np.quantile(finite, [1. / 3., 2. / 3.])\\\\n    labels = np.searchsorted(thresholds, values, side='right').astype(np.int64)\\\\n    return labels, thresholds\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef trial_number_in_block(probability_left):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"0-based index of each trial within its block of constant `probabilityLeft`.\\\\n\\\\n    Computed on the *complete* trials table before any trial is excluded, so that the\\\\n    numbering reflects the block structure the mouse actually experienced (the IBL task has\\\\n    an initial 90-trial unbiased block at pLeft = 0.5, then blocks of 20-100 trials\\\\n    alternating between pLeft = 0.8 and 0.2).\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    p = np.asarray(probability_left, dtype=float)\\\\n    new_block = np.ones(len(p), dtype=bool)\\\\n    if len(p) > 1:\\\\n        # NaN != NaN, so a NaN pLeft always starts a new block; those trials are excluded\\\\n        # later by the trials mask anyway.\\\\n        new_block[1:] = ~(p[1:] == p[:-1])\\\\n    block_id = np.cumsum(new_block) - 1\\\\n    # index within block = running count restarting at each block boundary\\\\n    starts = np.nonzero(new_block)[0]\\\\n    within = np.arange(len(p)) - starts[block_id]\\\\n    return within.astype(np.float32), block_id\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\\\n# Per-session conversion\\\\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\\\ndef convert_session(eid, verbose=True, collect_debug=False):\\\\n    \\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"Convert one session. Returns a dict, or raises on failure.\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n    timing = {}\\\\n    one = get_one()\\\\n    brain_regions = BrainRegions()\\\\n\\\\n    t = time.time()\\\\n    pids, pnames = one.eid2pid(eid)\\\\n    timing['eid2pid'] = time.time() - t\\\\n\\\\n    # ---- neural -----------------------------------------------------------------\\\\n    t = time.time()\\\\n    spikes, clusters = load_session_spikes(one, eid, pids, pnames)\\\\n    timing['load_spikes'] = time.time() - t\\\\n    n_clusters_all = len(clusters)\\\\n\\\\n    t = time.time()\\\\n    keep_idx, beryl_keep = select_neurons(clusters, brain_regions)\\\\n    n_neurons = len(keep_idx)\\\\n    if n_neurons == 0:\\\\n        raise RuntimeError('no well-isolated grey-matter neurons')\\\\n    remap = np.full(n_clusters_all, -1, dtype=np.int64)\\\\n    remap[keep_idx] = np.arange(n_neurons)\\\\n    sc = remap[spikes['clusters']]\\\\n    sel = sc >= 0\\\\n    spike_times = np.ascontiguousarray(spikes['times'][sel])\\\\n    spike_clusters = np.ascontiguousarray(sc[sel])\\\\n    timing['select_neurons'] = time.time() - t\\\\n\\\\n    # ---- trials -----------------------------------------------------------------\\\\n    t = time.time()\\\\n    sess_loader = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)\\\\n    # `load_trials_and_mask` builds the data paper's trial exclusion mask. Note the\\\\n    # reference calls `SessionLoader(one, eid)` positionally, which ibllib 4.0.1 no longer\\\\n    # accepts, hence passing an explicit `sess_loader`.\\\\n    trials, mask = load_trials_and_mask(\\\\n        one=one, eid=eid, max_trial_len=MAX_TRIAL_LEN, sess_loader=sess_loader)\\\\n    mask = np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool)\\\\n    timing['load_trials'] = time.time() - t\\\\n    n_trials_all = len(trials)\\\\n\\\\n    align_times = trials[ALIGN_TIME].to_numpy()\\\\n    in_block, _ = trial_number_in_block(trials['probabilityLeft'].to_numpy())\\\\n\\\\n    # ---- behaviour --------------------------------------------------------------\\\\n    t = time.time()\\\\n    beh_traces, camera_used = load_dynamic_behaviour(sess_loader)\\\\n    timing['load_behaviour'] = time.time() - t\\\\n\\\\n    t = time.time()\\\\n    wheel_vals, wheel_ok = bin_behaviour_per_trial(*beh_traces['wheel-speed'], align_times)\\\\n    me_vals, me_ok = bin_behaviour_per_trial(*beh_traces['whisker-motion-energy'], align_times)\\\\n    timing['bin_behaviour'] = time.time() - t\\\\n\\\\n    # ---- trial selection ---------------------------------------------------------\\\\n    # Mirrors `align_spike_behavior`: keep trials that pass the trials mask AND for which\\\\n    # every behavioural trace could be extracted.\\\\n    keep_trials = mask & wheel_ok & me_ok\\\\n    n_keep = int(keep_trials.sum())\\\\n    if n_keep < MIN_TRIALS:\\\\n        raise RuntimeError(f'only {n_keep} usable trials')\\\\n\\\\n    # ---- bin spikes (only for the trials we keep) --------------------------------\\\\n    t = time.time()\\\\n    binned = bin_spiking_data_fast(spike_times, spike_clusters, n_neurons,\\\\n                                   align_times[keep_trials])\\\\n    timing['bin_spikes'] = time.time() - t\\\\n\\\\n    # ---- inputs ------------------------------------------------------------------\\\\n    tr = trials[keep_trials]\\\\n    inp = np.empty((n_keep, 2, NBINS), dtype=np.float32)\\\\n    inp[:, 0, :] = BIN_CENTRES.astype(np.float32)\\\\n    inp[:, 1, :] = in_block[keep_trials][:, None]\\\\n\\\\n    # ---- outputs -----------------------------------------------------------------\\\\n    # choice: IBL codes +1 / -1. Verified empirically (see CONVERSION_NOTES Step 4):\\\\n    # on correct trials with the stimulus on the left, choice == +1; on correct trials with\\\\n    # the stimulus on the right, choice == -1. So +1 is a leftward choice.\\\\n    choice = tr['choice'].to_numpy()\\\\n    choice_out = (choice < 0).astype(np.int64)          # left -> 0, right -> 1\\\\n\\\\n    pleft = tr['probabilityLeft'].to_numpy()\\\\n    prior_out = np.full(n_keep, -1, dtype=np.int64)\\\\n    for value, code in ((0.2, 0), (0.5, 1), (0.8, 2)):\\\\n        prior_out[np.isclose(pleft, value)] = code\\\\n    if np.any(prior_out < 0):\\\\n        bad = np.unique(pleft[prior_out < 0])\\\\n        raise RuntimeError(f'unexpected probabilityLeft values {bad}')\\\\n\\\\n    wheel_kept = wheel_vals[keep_trials]\\\\n    me_kept = me_vals[keep_trials]\\\\n    wheel_lab, wheel_thr = discretize_tertiles(wheel_kept)\\\\n    me_lab, me_thr = discretize_tertiles(me_kept)\\\\n\\\\n    out = np.empty((n_keep, 4, NBINS), dtype=np.int64)\\\\n    out[:, 0, :] = choice_out[:, None]\\\\n    out[:, 1, :] = prior_out[:, None]\\\\n    out[:, 2, :] = wheel_lab\\\\n    out[:, 3, :] = me_lab\\\\n\\\\n    result = dict(\\\\n        eid=str(eid),\\\\n        neural=binned,                      # uint8 (n_keep, n_neurons, NBINS)\\\\n        input=inp,\\\\n        output=out,\\\\n        beryl=beryl_keep,\\\\n        n_clusters_all=int(n_clusters_all),\\\\n        n_good_all=int((clusters['label'].to_numpy() >= QC_LABEL).sum()),\\\\n        n_neurons=int(n_neurons),\\\\n        n_probes=len(pids),\\\\n        n_trials_all=int(n_trials_all),\\\\n        n_trials_mask=int(mask.sum()),\\\\n        n_trials_kept=n_keep,\\\\n        camera_used=camera_used,\\\\n        wheel_thresholds=wheel_thr,\\\\n        me_thresholds=me_thr,\\\\n        frac_correct=float((trials['feedbackType'].to_numpy() == 1).mean()),\\\\n        timing=timing,\\\\n    )\\\\n    if collect_debug:\\\\n        result['debug'] = dict(\\\\n            trials=trials, mask=mask, keep_trials=keep_trials,\\\\n            align_times=align_times, in_block=in_block,\\\\n            wheel_trace=beh_traces['wheel-speed'], me_trace=beh_traces['whisker-motion-energy'],\\\\n            wheel_vals=wheel_kept, me_vals=me_kept,\\\\n            spike_times=spike_times, spike_clusters=spike_clusters,\\\\n        )\\\\n    if verbose:\\\\n        print(f'  [{eid}] probes={len(pids)} clusters={n_clusters_all} '\\\\n              f'good={result[\\\\\\\"n_good_all\\\\\\\"]} kept_neurons={n_neurons} '\\\\n              f'trials={n_trials_all}->mask {int(mask.sum())}->kept {n_keep} '\\\\n              f'camera={camera_used} '\\\\n              f'({sum(timing.values()):.1f}s)', flush=True)\\\\n    return result\\\\n\\\\n\\\\ndef _worker(eid):\\\\n    try:\\\\n        return convert_session(eid, verbose=True)\\\\n    except Exception as exc:       # noqa: BLE001 -- one bad session must not kill the run\\\\n        return {'eid': str(eid), 'error': f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}',\\\\n                'traceback': traceback.format_exc()}\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\\\n# Diagnostic plots\\\\n# = spike_times[i0[k]:i1[k]]\\n        c = spike_clusters[i0[k]:i1[k]]\\n        b = np.floor((t - beg[k]) / BINSIZE).astype(np.int64)\\n        ok = (b >= 0) & (b < NBINS)\\n        counts = np.bincount(c[ok] * NBINS + b[ok], minlength=n_clusters * NBINS)\\n        np.clip(counts, 0, 255, out=counts)\\n        out[k] = counts.reshape(n_clusters, NBINS).astype(np.uint8)\\n    return out\\n\\n\\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n# Behaviour\\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\ndef load_dynamic_behaviour(sess_loader):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Load the two time-varying behaviours the decoder has to predict.\\n\\n    Reproduces `ibl_data_utils.load_target_behavior`:\\n      * wheel speed  = |velocity| of the uniformly resampled (~1 kHz) wheel trace,\\n      * whisker motion energy = `whiskerMotionEnergy` of the **left** camera (60 Hz),\\n        falling back to the right camera (150 Hz) when the left one is unavailable --\\n        exactly the fallback in `ibl_data_utils.bin_behaviors`.\\n\\n    Returns {'wheel-speed': (times, values), 'whisker-motion-energy': (times, values)},\\n    plus the camera actually used.\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    out = {}\\n    sess_loader.load_wheel()\\n    out['wheel-speed'] = (sess_loader.wheel['times'].to_numpy(),\\n                          np.abs(sess_loader.wheel['velocity'].to_numpy()))\\n\\n    camera_used = None\\n    for view, key in (('left', 'leftCamera'), ('right', 'rightCamera')):\\n        try:\\n            sess_loader.load_motion_energy(views=[view])\\n            me = sess_loader.motion_energy[key]\\n            times = me['times'].to_numpy()\\n            vals = me['whiskerMotionEnergy'].to_numpy()\\n            if len(times) == 0 or np.all(np.isnan(vals)):\\n                continue\\n            out['whisker-motion-energy'] = (times, vals)\\n            camera_used = view\\n            break\\n        except Exception:\\n            continue\\n    if camera_used is None:\\n        raise RuntimeError('no whisker motion energy available')\\n    return out, camera_used\\n\\n\\ndef bin_behaviour_per_trial(target_times, target_vals, align_times):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Resample a behavioural trace onto the 100 trial bins, per trial.\\n\\n    Faithful re-implementation of `ibl_data_utils.get_behavior_per_interval`:\\n      * the trace is sliced to the open interval (t_beg, t_end),\\n      * a trial is rejected when there is no data, when the trace starts more than one bin\\n        after `t_beg` or ends more than one bin before `t_end`, when the interval time is\\n        NaN, or when the slice contains NaNs,\\n      * the remaining trials are linearly interpolated (with linear extrapolation at the\\n        edges) onto `np.linspace(t_beg + binsize, t_end, n_bins)`, i.e. the right edge of\\n        each bin.\\n\\n    The only deviation is that NaNs always reject a trial (the reference's\\n    `allow_nans=False` branch). The reference caching script passes `allow_nans=True` and\\n    lets the model impute NaNs with the trial average at fit time; here the converted\\n    outputs must be valid class labels at every timepoint, and `verify_data_format`\\n    rejects NaNs outright, so NaN-containing trials are dropped instead.\\n\\n    Returns (values (n_trials, NBINS) float64 with NaN rows for rejected trials,\\n             good mask (n_trials,) bool).\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    n = len(align_times)\\n    vals = np.full((n, NBINS), np.nan)\\n    good = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)\\n\\n    beg = align_times + TIME_WINDOW[0]\\n    end = align_times + TIME_WINDOW[1]\\n    finite = np.isfinite(beg) & np.isfinite(end)\\n    if not np.any(finite):\\n        return vals, good\\n\\n    idx_beg = np.searchsorted(target_times, np.where(finite, beg, np.inf), side='right')\\n    idx_end = np.searchsorted(target_times, np.where(finite, end, np.inf), side='left')\\n\\n    for k in range(n):\\n        if not finite[k]:\\n            continue\\n        tt = target_times[idx_beg[k]:idx_end[k]]\\n        tv = target_vals[idx_beg[k]:idx_end[k]]\\n        if len(tv) == 0:\\n            continue\\n        if np.isnan(tv).any():\\n            continue\\n        if abs(beg[k] - tt[0]) > BINSIZE:      # target data starts too late\\n            continue\\n        if abs(end[k] - tt[-1]) > BINSIZE:     # target data ends too early\\n            continue\\n        x = np.linspace(beg[k] + BINSIZE, end[k], NBINS)\\n        vals[k] = interp1d(tt, tv, kind='linear', fill_value='extrapolate')(x)\\n        good[k] = True\\n    return vals, good\\n\\n\\ndef discretize_tertiles(values):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Discretize a continuous time-varying behaviour into 3 equal-occupancy bins.\\n\\n    Thresholds are the 33.3rd and 66.7th percentiles of every retained (trial, time-bin)\\n    sample of **that session**. Per-session thresholds are used because both signals are in\\n    session-specific units: whisker motion energy is an uncalibrated pixel-intensity\\n    difference whose scale depends on the camera (left 1280x1024 @60 Hz vs right 640x512\\n    @150 Hz), on illumination and on ROI placement, and wheel-speed statistics depend on how\\n    vigorously a given mouse turns the wheel. A single global threshold would map whole\\n    sessions into one class; per-session tertiles give ~1/3 of samples per class in every\\n    session, so chance is a well-defined 1/3 and the shared decoder sees a comparable\\n    target in every session.\\n\\n    Returns (labels (int) in {0,1,2}, thresholds (2,)).\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    finite = values[np.isfinite(values)]\\n    thresholds = np.quantile(finite, [1. / 3., 2. / 3.])\\n    labels = np.searchsorted(thresholds, values, side='right').astype(np.int64)\\n    return labels, thresholds\\n\\n\\ndef trial_number_in_block(probability_left):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"0-based index of each trial within its block of constant `probabilityLeft`.\\n\\n    Computed on the *complete* trials table before any trial is excluded, so that the\\n    numbering reflects the block structure the mouse actually experienced (the IBL task has\\n    an initial 90-trial unbiased block at pLeft = 0.5, then blocks of 20-100 trials\\n    alternating between pLeft = 0.8 and 0.2).\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    p = np.asarray(probability_left, dtype=float)\\n    new_block = np.ones(len(p), dtype=bool)\\n    if len(p) > 1:\\n        # NaN != NaN, so a NaN pLeft always starts a new block; those trials are excluded\\n        # later by the trials mask anyway.\\n        new_block[1:] = ~(p[1:] == p[:-1])\\n    block_id = np.cumsum(new_block) - 1\\n    # index within block = running count restarting at each block boundary\\n    starts = np.nonzero(new_block)[0]\\n    within = np.arange(len(p)) - starts[block_id]\\n    return within.astype(np.float32), block_id\\n\\n\\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\n# Per-session conversion\\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\ndef convert_session(eid, verbose=True, collect_debug=False):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Convert one session. Returns a dict, or raises on failure.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    timing = {}\\n    one = get_one()\\n    brain_regions = BrainRegions()\\n\\n    t = time.time()\\n    pids, pnames = one.eid2pid(eid)\\n    timing['eid2pid'] = time.time() - t\\n\\n    # ---- neural -----------------------------------------------------------------\\n    t = time.time()\\n    spikes, clusters = load_session_spikes(one, eid, pids, pnames)\\n    timing['load_spikes'] = time.time() - t\\n    n_clusters_all = len(clusters)\\n\\n    t = time.time()\\n    keep_idx, beryl_keep = select_neurons(clusters, brain_regions)\\n    n_neurons = len(keep_idx)\\n    if n_neurons == 0:\\n        raise RuntimeError('no well-isolated grey-matter neurons')\\n    remap = np.full(n_clusters_all, -1, dtype=np.int64)\\n    remap[keep_idx] = np.arange(n_neurons)\\n    sc = remap[spikes['clusters']]\\n    sel = sc >= 0\\n    spike_times = np.ascontiguousarray(spikes['times'][sel])\\n    spike_clusters = np.ascontiguousarray(sc[sel])\\n    timing['select_neurons'] = time.time() - t\\n\\n    # ---- trials -----------------------------------------------------------------\\n    t = time.time()\\n    sess_loader = SessionLoader(one=one, eid=eid)\\n    # `load_trials_and_mask` builds the data paper's trial exclusion mask. Note the\\n    # reference calls `SessionLoader(one, eid)` positionally, which ibllib 4.0.1 no longer\\n    # accepts, hence passing an explicit `sess_loader`.\\n    trials, mask = load_trials_and_mask(\\n        one=one, eid=eid, max_trial_len=MAX_TRIAL_LEN, sess_loader=sess_loader)\\n    mask = np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool)\\n    timing['load_trials'] = time.time() - t\\n    n_trials_all = len(trials)\\n\\n    align_times = trials[ALIGN_TIME].to_numpy()\\n    in_block, _ = trial_number_in_block(trials['probabilityLeft'].to_numpy())\\n\\n    # ---- behaviour --------------------------------------------------------------\\n    t = time.time()\\n    beh_traces, camera_used = load_dynamic_behaviour(sess_loader)\\n    timing['load_behaviour'] = time.time() - t\\n\\n    t = time.time()\\n    wheel_vals, wheel_ok = bin_behaviour_per_trial(*beh_traces['wheel-speed'], align_times)\\n    me_vals, me_ok = bin_behaviour_per_trial(*beh_traces['whisker-motion-energy'], align_times)\\n    timing['bin_behaviour'] = time.time() - t\\n\\n    # ---- trial selection ---------------------------------------------------------\\n    # Mirrors `align_spike_behavior`: keep trials that pass the trials mask AND for which\\n    # every behavioural trace could be extracted.\\n    keep_trials = mask & wheel_ok & me_ok\\n    n_keep = int(keep_trials.sum())\\n    if n_keep < MIN_TRIALS:\\n        raise RuntimeError(f'only {n_keep} usable trials')\\n\\n    # ---- bin spikes (only for the trials we keep) --------------------------------\\n    t = time.time()\\n    binned = bin_spiking_data_fast(spike_times, spike_clusters, n_neurons,\\n                                   align_times[keep_trials])\\n    timing['bin_spikes'] = time.time() - t\\n\\n    # ---- inputs ------------------------------------------------------------------\\n    tr = trials[keep_trials]\\n    inp = np.empty((n_keep, 2, NBINS), dtype=np.float32)\\n    inp[:, 0, :] = BIN_CENTRES.astype(np.float32)\\n    inp[:, 1, :] = in_block[keep_trials][:, None]\\n\\n    # ---- outputs -----------------------------------------------------------------\\n    # choice: IBL codes +1 / -1. Verified empirically (see CONVERSION_NOTES Step 4):\\n    # on correct trials with the stimulus on the left, choice == +1; on correct trials with\\n    # the stimulus on the right, choice == -1. So +1 is a leftward choice.\\n    choice = tr['choice'].to_numpy()\\n    choice_out = (choice < 0).astype(np.int64)          # left -> 0, right -> 1\\n\\n    pleft = tr['probabilityLeft'].to_numpy()\\n    prior_out = np.full(n_keep, -1, dtype=np.int64)\\n    for value, code in ((0.2, 0), (0.5, 1), (0.8, 2)):\\n        prior_out[np.isclose(pleft, value)] = code\\n    if np.any(prior_out < 0):\\n        bad = np.unique(pleft[prior_out < 0])\\n        raise RuntimeError(f'unexpected probabilityLeft values {bad}')\\n\\n    wheel_kept = wheel_vals[keep_trials]\\n    me_kept = me_vals[keep_trials]\\n    wheel_lab, wheel_thr = discretize_tertiles(wheel_kept)\\n    me_lab, me_thr = discretize_tertiles(me_kept)\\n\\n    out = np.empty((n_keep, 4, NBINS), dtype=np.int64)\\n    out[:, 0, :] = choice_out[:, None]\\n    out[:, 1, :] = prior_out[:, None]\\n    out[:, 2, :] = wheel_lab\\n    out[:, 3, :] = me_lab\\n\\n    result = dict(\\n        eid=str(eid),\\n        neural=binned,                      # uint8 (n_keep, n_neurons, NBINS)\\n        input=inp,\\n        output=out,\\n        beryl=beryl_keep,\\n        n_clusters_all=int(n_clusters_all),\\n        n_good_all=int((clusters['label'].to_numpy() >= QC_LABEL).sum()),\\n        n_neurons=int(n_neurons),\\n        n_probes=len(pids),\\n        n_trials_all=int(n_trials_all),\\n        n_trials_mask=int(mask.sum()),\\n        n_trials_kept=n_keep,\\n        camera_used=camera_used,\\n        wheel_thresholds=wheel_thr,\\n        me_thresholds=me_thr,\\n        frac_correct=float((trials['feedbackType'].to_numpy() == 1).mean()),\\n        timing=timing,\\n    )\\n    if collect_debug:\\n        result['debug'] = dict(\\n            trials=trials, mask=mask, keep_trials=keep_trials,\\n            align_times=align_times, in_block=in_block,\\n            wheel_trace=beh_traces['wheel-speed'], me_trace=beh_traces['whisker-motion-energy'],\\n            wheel_vals=wheel_kept, me_vals=me_kept,\\n            spike_times=spike_times, spike_clusters=spike_clusters,\\n        )\\n    if verbose:\\n        print(f'  [{eid}] probes={len(pids)} clusters={n_clusters_all} '\\n              f'good={result[\\\"n_good_all\\\"]} kept_neurons={n_neurons} '\\n              f'trials={n_trials_all}->mask {int(mask.sum())}->kept {n_keep} '\\n              f'camera={camera_used} '\\n              f'({sum(timing.values()):.1f}s)', flush=True)\\n    return result\\n\\n\\ndef _worker(eid):\\n    try:\\n        return convert_session(eid, verbose=True)\\n    except Exception as exc:       # noqa: BLE001 -- one bad session must not kill the run\\n        return {'eid': str(eid), 'error': f'{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}',\\n                'traceback': traceback.format_exc()}\\n\\n\\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\ndef main():\\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\\n    ap.add_argument('outfile', type=str, `_worker` wraps it so a single bad session\\n  cannot kill the run.\\n- `plot_processing` — the `--show-processing` figure.\\n- `main` — `ProcessPoolExecutor` fan-out over sessions, assembly, summary, pickle.\\n\\nThe reference `load_trials_and_mask` and `merge_probes` are **imported** from\\n`/app/code/code_zhang2025/src/utils/ibl_data_utils.py` rather than re-implemented.\\n\\nCode inefficiencies identified in the reference:\\n- `get_spike_data_per_interval` spawns a multiprocessing pool and calls `bincount2D`\\n  once per trial (≈600 pool tasks per session), each of which re-derives a cluster\\n  index with `np.intersect1d`.\\n- `get_behavior_per_interval` likewise uses a pool per behaviour per session.\\n- `load_anytime_behaviors` loads six behavioural streams, four of which\\n  (wheel velocity, right whisker ME, both pupil diameters) the caching script never uses.\\n- `load_spiking_data` streams raw AP data just to read a sampling rate.\\n\\nCode speedups added:\\n- Spike binning vectorised with `searchsorted` + a single `np.bincount` per trial:\\n  ~0.02 s per session instead of seconds of pool overhead.\\n- Spikes are binned **only for the trials that survive curation**.\\n- Parallelism moved up to the session level (`ProcessPoolExecutor`, 32 workers), which is\\n  where the real cost (loading 200–500 MB `spikes.*.npy` per probe) lies.\\n- Only the two behaviours actually needed are loaded; no raw-ephys streaming.\\n- Spike counts are carried as `uint8` from the workers (the reference stores `np.ubyte`\\n  too) and expanded to `float32` once, in the parent.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step 7: Sample Conversion and Validation\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\n\\n`python -u /app/convert_data.py /app/sample_data.pkl --sample --show-processing`\\n→ `/app/conversion_sample_out.txt`, `/app/sample_data.pkl`,\\n`/app/processing_<eid>.png` (2 files).\\n\\n### Sample Statistics\\n| Statistic | Value |\\n|-----------|-------|\\n| Sessions | 2 |\\n| Neurons (total) | 253 |\\n| Neurons / session | 61, 192 (mean 126.5) |\\n| Subjects | 1 (NYU-11) |\\n| Sessions / subject | 2 |\\n| Trials (total) | 651 |\\n| Trials / session | 407, 244 |\\n| All clusters / probe | 875.3 (datapaper: 889) |\\n| Good clusters / probe | 113.3 (datapaper: 108) |\\n| Fraction correct | 0.854 |\\n| `time_from_stimulus_onset` range | [−0.49, 1.49] |\\n| `trial_number_in_block` range | [0, 89] |\\n| choice distribution | left 0.518, right 0.482 |\\n| prior distribution | 0.2 → 0.478, 0.5 → 0.161, 0.8 → 0.361 |\\n| wheel speed distribution | 0.333 / 0.333 / 0.333 |\\n| whisker ME distribution | 0.333 / 0.333 / 0.333 |\\n\\n### Processing Plots Review\\n`processing_6713a4a7-….png` (7 rows of panels) shows:\\n1. the only substantive addition is the data\\npaper's neuron QC + grey-matter restriction, which the method-paper code omits.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step 5: Mapping Planning\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\n\\n### Variable Mapping\\n| Source (ONE object.attribute) | Target field | Transform | Reference code function(s) | Notes |\\n|---|---|---|---|---|\\n| `spikes.times`, `spikes.clusters` (all probes) + `clusters.label`, `clusters.acronym` | `neural[session][trial]` (n_neurons, 100) float32 | pool probes → keep `label>=1` & Beryl ∉ {root, void} → count spikes in 100 × 20 ms bins over `stimOn_times + (-0.5, 1.5)` | `prepare_data`, `load_spiking_data`, `merge_probes`, `list_brain_regions`, `select_brain_regions`, `bin_spiking_data` | spike **counts**, not rates, matching the reference cached dataset |\\n| bin index | `input[…][0]` | signed bin-centre time, −0.49 … +1.49 s | — (task spec: \\\"time since stimulus onset, continuous, time-varying\\\") | constant grid, identical for every trial |\\n| `trials.probabilityLeft` | `input[…][1]` | 0-based index of the trial within its run of constant `probabilityLeft`, computed on the **unfiltered** trials table, broadcast over the 100 bins | — (task spec: \\\"trial number in block, continuous, per-trial\\\") | block structure must come from all trials, not the filtered subset |\\n| `trials.choice` | `output[…][0]` | `+1 → 0` (left), `−1 → 1` (right); `0` (no response) already excluded | `bin_behaviors` (`choice`) | direction verified empirically, see sanity checks |\\n| `trials.probabilityLeft` | `output[…][1]` | `0.2 → 0`, `0.5 → 1`, `0.8 → 2` | `bin_behaviors` (`block`) | exactly as required by the task spec |\\n| `wheel.velocity` (SessionLoader, ~1 kHz resampled) | `output[…][2]` | `abs(velocity)` → interpolate onto the right edge of each 20 ms bin → per-session tertiles → {0,1,2} | `load_target_behavior('wheel-speed')`, `get_behavior_per_interval` | time-varying |\\n| `leftCamera.ROIMotionEnergy` (`whiskerMotionEnergy`, 60 Hz; right camera fallback) | `output[…][3]` | interpolate onto bin right edges → per-session tertiles → {0,1,2} | `load_target_behavior('left-whisker-motion-energy')`, fallback logic in `bin_behaviors` | time-varying |\\n| `clusters.acronym` → Beryl | `brain_regions`, `brain_region_idx` | `BrainRegions().acronym2acronym(..., mapping='Beryl')` | `list_brain_regions` | |\\n| `bwm_release.csv` `subject` | `subjects`, `subject_idx` | unique sorted subject names | `0_data_caching.py` | |\\n\\n### Key Decisions\\n1. **Alignment = `stimOn_times`, window (−0.5, +1.5) s, 20 ms bins (T = 100).** Exactly the\\n   reference `params`; also what the task specification requires.\\n2. **Spike counts, unnormalised.** The reference caches raw counts (`np.ubyte`) and\\n   z-scores only inside the model (`standardize_spike_data`). `train_decoder.py` does its\\n   own SVD-based projection, so raw counts are the right thing to store.\\n3. **Neuron QC: `label >= 1` + grey matter.** See Step 4. Sanity check: this must give\\n   ≈108 neurons per probe and ≈62–63k neurons in total.\\n4. **Trial QC: reference `load_trials_and_mask(max_trial_len=10.0)`**, imported directly\\n   from the reference module so the logic cannot drift.\\n5. **Behaviour-coverage QC.** A trial is dropped when the wheel or whisker trace does not\\n   cover the whole 2 s window (the reference's \\\"target data starts too late / ends too\\n   early\\\" tests) or contains NaN.\\n6. **Ephys-coverage QC (addition).** A trial is dropped when its window intersects a\\n   >0.5 s gap in the *pooled unfiltered* spike train or falls outside the recorded\\n   interval. Necessary because some sessions keep running the behavioural rig after the\\n   ephys stops; those trials would otherwise be all-zero.\\n7. **Session QC: ≥5 well-isolated grey-matter neurons** (the data paper's per-session\\n   neuron minimum), a usable whisker trace, and ≥2 usable trials.\\n8. **Per-session tertiles for the two continuous outputs.** Both signals are in\\n   session-specific units (motion energy is an uncalibrated pixel difference that depends\\n   on camera resolution/frame rate, illumination and ROI placement; wheel speed depends on\\n   how vigorously the individual mouse turns). Per-session tertiles make chance exactly\\n   1/3 in every session and give the *shared* decoder a comparable target everywhere. A\\n   single global threshold would push whole sessions into one class.\\n9. **Both inputs and all four outputs are stored time-varying (d, 100)**, per-trial\\n   variables being broadcast along time, as the format instructions prefer.\\n10. **Session order** follows `bwm_release.csv`, so the conversion is deterministic.\\n\\n### Planned Sanity Checks\\n- [x] all clusters/probe ≈ 889 (datapaper)\\n- [x] well-isolated clusters/probe ≈ 108 (datapaper)\\n- [x] raw trials/session: mean ≈ 645, median ≈ 602, range 401–1525 (datapaper)\\n- [x] fraction correct ≈ 0.814 (datapaper)\\n- [x] 459 eids / 699 pids / 139 subjects in the freeze file (datapaper)\\n- [x] number of retained sessions in the ballpark of the method paper's 433\\n- [x] number of Beryl regions in the ballpark of the method paper's 270\\n- [x] total well-isolated grey-matter neurons ≈ the data paper's canonical 62,857\\n- [x] `probabilityLeft` only ever 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.8, first block = 90 trials at 0.5\\n- [x] population PSTH shows a stimulus-locked transient starting at t = 0\\n- [x] wheel speed rises at `firstMovement_times` when trials are sorted by reaction time\\n- [x] tertile classes each hold ≈1/3 of timepoints\\n- [x] element-wise re-derivation of neural/input/output from the raw data (Step 10)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step 6: Script Development\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\n\\n`/app/convert_data.py`; runs as\\n`python -u /app/convert_data.py <out.pkl> [--full|--sample] [--show-processing] [--n-workers N]`.\\n\\nStructure:\\n- `get_one()` / `get_brain_regions()` — per-process singletons.\\n- `load_session_spikes` — brainbox `SpikeSortingLoader` per probe + reference `merge_probes`.\\n- `select_neurons` — `label >= 1` and Beryl ∉ {root, void}.\\n- `bin_spiking_data_fast` — vectorised replacement for the reference\\n  `bin_spiking_data`/`get_spike_data_per_interval`, bin-for-bin identical.\\n- `neural_data_available` — ephys-coverage mask.\\n- `load_dynamic_behaviour` — reference `load_target_behavior` logic (wheel speed, whisker ME).\\n- `bin_behaviour_per_trial` — faithful re-implementation of `get_behavior_per_interval`.\\n- `discretize_tertiles`, `trial_number_in_block`.\\n- `convert_session` — the per-session pipeline; `_worker` wraps it so a single bad session\\n  cannot kill the run.\\n- `plot_processing` — the `--show-processing` figure.\\n- `main` — `ProcessPoolExecutor` fan-out over sessions, assembly, summary, pickle.\\n\\nThe reference `load_trials_and_mask` and `merge_probes` are **imported** from\\n`/app/code/code_zhang2025/src/utils/ibl_data_utils.py` rather than re-implemented.\\n\\nCode inefficiencies identified in the reference:\\n- `get_spike_data_per_interval` spawns a multiprocessing pool and calls `bincount2D`\\n  once per trial (≈600 pool tasks per session), each of which re-derives a cluster\\n  index with `np.intersect1d`.\\n- `get_behavior_per_interval` likewise uses a pool per behaviour per session.\\n- `load_anytime_behaviors` loads six behavioural streams, four of which\\n  (wheel velocity, right whisker ME, both pupil diameters) the caching script never uses.\\n- `load_spiking_data` streams raw AP data just to read a sampling rate.\\n\\nCode speedups added:\\n- Spike binning vectorised with `searchsorted` + a single `np.bincount` per trial:\\n  ~0.02 s per session instead of seconds of pool overhead.\\n- Spikes are binned **only for the trials that survive curation**.\\n- Parallelism moved up to the session level (`ProcessPoolExecutor`, 32 workers), which is\\n  where the real cost (loading 200–500 MB `spikes.*.npy` per probe) lies.\\n- Only the two behaviours actually needed are loaded; no raw-ephys streaming.\\n- Spike counts are carried as `uint8` from the workers (the reference stores `np.ubyte`\\n  too) and expanded to `float32` once, in the parent.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step 7: Sample Conversion and Validation\\n**Status**: COMPLETE\\n\\n`python -u /app/convert_data.py /app/sample_data.pkl --sample --show-processing`\\n→ `/app/conversion_sample_out.txt`, `/app/sample_data.pkl`,\\n`/app/processing_<eid>.png` (2 files).\\n\\n### Sample Statistics\\n| Statistic | Value |\\n|-----------|-------|\\n| Sessions | 2 |\\n| Neurons (total) | 253 |\\n| Neurons / session | 61, 192 (mean 126.5) |\\n| Subjects | 1 (NYU-11) |\\n| Sessions / subject | 2 |\\n| Trials (total) | 651 |\\n| Trials / session | 407, 244 |\\n| All clusters / probe | 875.3 (datapaper: 889) |\\n| Good clusters / probe | 113.3 (datapaper: 108) |\\n| Fraction correct | 0.854 |\\n| `time_from_stimulus_onset` range | [−0.49, 1.49] |\\n| `trial_number_in_block` range | [0, 89] |\\n| choice distribution | left 0.518, right 0.482 |\\n| prior distribution | 0.2 → 0.478, 0.5 → 0.161, 0.8 → 0.361 |\\n| wheel speed distribution | 0.333 / 0.333 / 0.333 |\\n| whisker ME distribution | 0.333 / 0.333 / 0.333 |\\n\\n### Processing Plots Review\\n`processing_6713a4a7-….png` (7 rows of panels) shows:\\n1. its run of constant `probabilityLeft`, counted on the *complete* trials table |\\n\\n### Outputs (`output_names`, `output_values`)\\n\\n| i | Name | Kind | Classes | Definition `reference_code`, dataset totals,\\n`failed_sessions`, and `session_info` — one record per session with the eid, subject, lab,\\ndate, probe/cluster/neuron counts, trial counts at each curation stage,
